UX-NAV-004.how: Both irreversible one-click actions now ask, and the one that had no undo got one. dashboard.html: 'Off for today' no longer POSTs on click; it swaps itself for 'Yes, stop until tomorrow' / 'Keep going' (standdownAsk, dashboard.html:270), and a new 'Resume today' button (dashboard.html:170) appears exactly while h.stoodDownForDay is true and clears it through a new POST /api/standdown/clear (lib/server.js:532) backed by Engine.resumeDay() (lib/engine.js:280), which resets stoodDownForDay and standDownDate and logs a stand_down_cleared event. panel.html: 'Try again' now only opens a confirm step (#reader-retry-confirm, panel.html:567) naming what is discarded; 'Discard it and reopen' (panel.html:572) is what actually POSTs /api/reading/retry.
UX-NAV-004.verified: Playwright against a real second instance of lib/server.js with a real Engine (persist:false), so the live daemon was never restarted. Click 'Off for today': {"offHidden":true,"yes":"Yes, stop until tomorrow","yesShown":true,"noShown":true,"standdownPosts":[]} — zero POSTs fired. 'Keep going': {"standdownPosts":[]}. Confirming: {"live":"Watching. up 3s · 0 gaps · 0 delivered · stood down for today","resumeShown":true,"offHidden":true,"engineStoodDownForDay":true,"engineDate":"2026-08-20"}. Then 'Resume today': {"resumeShown":false,"offShown":true,"engineStoodDownForDay":false,"engineDate":null,"postsSeen":["/api/standdown","/api/standdown/clear"]}. Route alone, straight at the server: POST /api/standdown {day:true} -> {"ok":true,"forDay":true}; stoodDownForDay = true | standDownDate = 2026-08-20; POST /api/standdown/clear -> 200 {"ok":true,"wasStoodDown":true}; stoodDownForDay = false | standDownDate = null. Panel side: {"confirmShown":true,"tryAgainHidden":true,"question":"Reopening throws away the device registration Amazon has stored here. Your sign-in stays, ","postsFired":0}, then {"tryAgainBack":true,"postsFired":0}, then postsFired 1 only after 'Discard it and reopen'.

UX-THEME-004.how: Two new tokens and two raised ones, all measured rather than judged. --on-accent (#FFFFFF light, #0E1116 dark) replaces the hardcoded #fff on every filled accent button (panel.html:339 and :126, dashboard.html:85). --edge (#6D8298 light, #5A6B82 dark) replaces --rule as the sole boundary of interactive components: button.act, #companions .top button, .reader-menu and textarea in panel.html, and `button` in dashboard.html; --rule stays what it always was, a divider. --faint went #8B96A3 -> #5E6977 (light) and #6C7784 -> #7B8693 (dark). --warn went to #96580D (light), which also lifts it clear on --sunk. The same token block is carried in web/debug.html, so --faint and --warn were synced there too.

UX-COPY-005.how: The raw upstream string is now mapped. A new ankiRemedy() (panel.html:766) turns each of the four AnkiConnect failures into the next move, and the string Anki actually returned stays on screen beneath it in .mono, so the remedy can be checked rather than taken on faith (panel.html:801). The five bare errors each name a next step: 'Cards did not load. The daemon did not answer: start it with interstice start, then press Cards again.' (:836), 'That review was not recorded. Press the same ease button again.' (:934), 'The daemon stopped answering, so this page could not be read. Restart it with interstice start, then turn the page.' (:1178), 'Your book did not load. Open the Kindle app once, then press Book again.' (:1598), 'Interstice could not read Notes. Open Notes once, then press To-do again.' (:1720).

UX-SL-008.how: Both false zeros became three-state loads. The star calendar gained _calLoading() (panel.html:2287), which paints 35 shimmer cells and a spinner in the count line before the fetch, and _calFailed() (panel.html:2297), which the catch and a non-ok status now route to: it says the stars could not be read and offers a 'Try again' that reloads the same month, instead of printing 'No stars earned this month yet.' about a request nobody answered. loadQueued() paints a shimmer placeholder before its fetch, checks r.ok, and replaces the swallowed `catch { /* daemon gone */ }` with a line naming the failure and saying nothing was lost.
